newsitem.title: UK: GRE HI profits hit by sterling strength.
newsitem.headline: GRE HI profits hit by sterling strength.

text.p: British composite insurer Guardian Royal Exchange Plc on Wednesday reported a fall in first half profits as competition and sterling continued to pressure results.

GRE chief executive John Robins said the company was now achieving rate increases in the private motor market sector but had not seen any rapid changes to competitive pressures in other major market sectors.
The UK was affected by strong competition and an increase in frequency in private motor and higher subsidence claims.
Trading profits for the first six months of the year fell to 105 million pounds from 137 million pounds in the same period last year.
Analysts had forecast profits of between 110 and 130 million stg.
Sterling accounted for 9.5 million pounds of the fall in profits. Investment income was reduced by 14.5 million pounds.
In Germany, GRE's second largest territory, pre-tax profits improved across all its units but profit translation was affected by the strength of sterling.
Taking account of investment income pretax profits rose to 502 million pounds from 231 million pounds last year.
The dividend was raised by 15 percent, above analyst expectations, to 3.9 pence per share.
Net asset value per share rose 11 percent to 311 pence per share.
Robins said GRE was actively seeking opportunities in areas it saw the greatest potential for sustained profitable business.
It was well-positioned to fund both organic and acquisition-led growth, he said, but stressed it would continue to adhere to its well established criteria for any acquisitions.
Restructuring in the UK was progressing well and planned cost reductions were being achieved, he added.

Over the year, total worldwide general insurance premium income fell to 1,501 million pounds from 1,544 million pounds again reflecting sterling strength and the sale in July 1996 of Guardian RE, the group's Swiss reinsurance company.
Life premiums were also down due to the currency and the run-off of the Nationwide Building Society business.

In the UK, Guardian Direct and RAC Insurance Direct had 778,000 policies in force at the end of June, an increase of 15 percent on the year-end figure. Average price increase of 10 percent were achieved over the period.
